 Chelsea find Alex Scott alternative – and it might be the smartest move they could make 
 Chelsea find Alex Scott alternative – and it might be the smartest move they could make
 22 Oct 2026 07:29 BST | 
 2 min read 
 Analysis 
 © IMAGO 
 Robin Bairner 
 | 
 Chief Editor 
 Make us your Google favourite 
 Chelsea were quoted a £100 million price for Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott , prompting interest in Brighton ’s rising star Yasin Ayari . Changing their transfer target could save the Blues millions and give them a better player. Here’s why.
 Article continues under the video Xabi Alonso’s side are hunting a new central midfield star, and while Scott has rapidly gained traction thanks to his strong performances for the Cherries, signing him promises to be a laborious task.
 Bournemouth have put a £100m tag on the England international, and while there is some justification in their stance due to the rarity of his profile, switching to Ayari, which TeamTalk suggests is a possibility, may prove a smarter long-term decision for the Stamford Bridge giants.

 Why Ayari and Scott are special talents
 Ayari and Scott both belong to a select group of midfielders who boast both a good current level and high long-term potential, according to data analytics firm SciSports’ SciSkill measure. This is calculated using hundreds of in-game data points.
 On top of this, they are part of an even more select group who are not cemented in the starting XIs at big clubs and who could, therefore, be available for transfer in 2027.
 2027's central midfielders to watch on the transfer market Name Club Age SciSkill Potential ETV (€m)

 Yegor Yarmolyuk Brentford 22 98.1 118.2 46.9 
 Nico Gonzalez Newcastle 24 103.3 116.7 35.0 
 Diego Gomez Brighton 23 102.1 116.5 6.7 
 Furthermore, the Sweden international is one of only three players on that list, along with Scott and Brentford’s Yegor Yarmolyuk, who are box-to-box players in their playing style.
 It’s worth noting here that Ayari is not only considered to be a better player than Scott currently, but he is projected to have a higher ceiling and has an Estimated Transfer Value (ETV) of approximately €20m less.
 The reasoning for Ayari’s lesser transfer fee is his contract situation. His deal with Brighton expires at the end of the season, though the Seagulls do have the option to extend it, and it must be assumed that they will. Nevertheless, the uncertainty over his long-term future is likely to keep his price down and the likelihood is that his price remains below Scott’s, despite his stronger rating.
 © IMAGO - Yasin Ayari, Brighton Chelsea in a strong position to negotiate a deal
 Ayari looks a good fit for Chelsea, who were left short of a central midfielder in the summer when they sold Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City but missed out Monaco’s Lamine Camara on a dramatic Deadline Day.
 In terms of playing time, style and formation, the Blues represent a strong fit for the 23-year-old, with doubts only lingering over his potential development.
 © IMAGO - Yasin Ayari, Chelsea Club Fit, October 2026 Chelsea stand a good chance of being able to overcome those concerns with the history attached to the club and the security that they can offer Ayari both in terms of contract size and lengthy.
 Ayari may not have the profile of Scott, but the evidence suggests he could be the smarter signing for the Blues.

 About us
 Our goal is simple - to become the #1 multi-language transfers source in the football world, serving the football fan their direct desire for everything around the most popular subject in football: Football Transfers.
 FootballTransfers (FT) is a project designed to fulfill the massive interest in the transfer market and provide a realistic, algorithmically-driven valuation of football players. We do this together with our partner SciSports .
 Valuing a player is currently an arbitrary process where teams, players and representatives simply estimate what they are worth. Together with SciSports, FT aims to use advanced football data, current and future skill level as well as contract length and other details to create our unique internal calculation. From there we derive our own valuation for each and every player in the world’s major football competitions.
